news.title: Because of the 2030 World Cup: Lekjaa takes an important decision regarding his position within CAF
news.lede: Fawzi Lekjaa looks set to reshuffle his cards within the Confederation of African Football. The move could bring an end to one of his most prominent roles in the corridors of African football, with the Moroccan moving towards resigning from the presidency of CAF's finance committee while keeping his position as first vice-president of the continental body. Moroccan website Hespport report that Lekjaa has decided to step down from the finance committee presidency because of the sheer weight of commitments the role brings. The frequent travel is part of it, as is the considerable time needed to follow up the various files tied to running CAF's financial affairs.

news.title: CAF sends message to Flamingos ahead of U-17 Women's World Cup final vs Japan
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has thrown its weight behind Nigeria's Flamingos ahead of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, scheduled for Saturday, November 7, in Morocco. Coach Akeem Busari's side made history by becoming the first African team to ever reach the final of the competition. Standing between Nigeria and the trophy is Japan, a side that already has one world title to their name.

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: Flamingos Captain Harmony Chidi Fires Warning to Japan Ahead of Final
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Nigeria's Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi has put Japan on notice, saying her side are ready to deliver a maiden FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title to the country when the two teams clash in Saturday's final in Rabat, Morocco. The match takes place at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 4, with kick-off set for 7:30 pm Nigerian time. It will be the first time Nigeria and Japan have faced each other at this stage of the competition.

news.title: FIFA partially upholds AFA's appeal against post World Cup sanctions; Nahuel's suspension reduced
news.lede: Zurich [Switzerland], November 7 (ANI): FIFA's Appeal Committee has partially upheld the Argentine Football Association (AFA) appeal against sanctions handed to several team members following the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, with Nahuel Molina's suspension getting reduced, while the punishment for midfielder Leandro Parades stands. As per a Spanish newspaper, Marca, report quoted by Goal.com, FIFA cut the ban for Nahuel from seven matches to four and also reduced his fine from 90,000 dollars to 60,000. But for Parades, his 10-match suspension along with his 90,000 dollar fine still stands. In an official statement, the AFA said that they would be requesting the grounds for decisions before taking them to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

news.title: Nigeria vs Japan: Where to watch FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final live

Nigeria's Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026 on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with kick-off scheduled for 7:30 PM at the Mohammed VI Complex Pitch-3 in Rabat, Morocco. The match will be the 52nd and final game of the tournament, and history will be made regardless of the result. As seen on FIFA's official website, it is the first time Nigeria and Japan have met at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup and the first time either country has faced the other in a World Cup final at any level.

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2026 final — Nigeria eyes history against heavyweight Japan
news.lede: Chennai Nigeria will look to script history in women’s football as it eyes its maiden title at the FIFA under-17 Women’s World Cup on Saturday. The Flamingos beat Brazil 3-1 in the semifinal and will be up against three-time finalist and Asian heavyweight Japan in a bid for the title in Rabat, Morocco. “From what we saw against DPR [Korea], I think it’s the core of what we should expect more of from the Japanese,” Nigeria coach Akeem Busari told FIFA at the final press conference. “But it’s a different ballgame because, for both us and them, the game will not be the same.

news.title: Argentina handed minor reprieve in World Cup final scuffle issue; Molina’s punishment reduced
news.lede: Chennai The Argentina Football Association announced on Friday that Argentina was granted a reprieve from sanctions against its defender, Nahuel Molina, due to his conduct during the final. After the FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Argentina and Spain, an altercation broke out between the players, with Leandro Paredes punching Pablo Martín Páez Gavira, which escalated into a full-blown scuffle. The FIFA Disciplinary Committee took note of the episode and announced the following sanctions against Argentine players and staff in August: Leandro Paredes (player): a 10 -match suspension and a fine of USD 90,000. Nahuel Molina (player): a seven-match suspension and a fine of USD 90,000.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.
